title: Prinsesstårta: Swedish Princess Cake with Raspberry, Custard and Marzipan Dome
summary: Light sponge layered with raspberry jam and vanilla custard, domed with whipped cream and covered in green marzipan with a pink marzipan rose.
equipment: two 20 cm round cake tins, greased and base-lined

ingredients.note: use ready-coloured green, or tint with a few drops of green gel colour

ingredients.item: tiny dab of pink gel food colouring, for the rose

steps.title: Cook the custard
steps.text: Whisk the sugar and cornflour in the saucepan, then whisk in the milk and yolks. Cook over medium heat, whisking steadily, for 5-7 min until it bubbles and thickens. Off the heat whisk in the butter and vanilla, sieve into a bowl, press cling film onto the surface and chill for at least 3 h. Letting it bubble fully activates the cornflour, so it sets without any gelatine.

steps.title: Prepare the oven
steps.text: Heat the oven to 180 °C (160 °C fan) and grease and base-line the two tins.

steps.title: Whisk the sponge
steps.text: Set the mixer bowl with the eggs, yolks and caster sugar over the simmering water and whisk until it reaches 43 °C, about 2-3 min. Move it to the mixer and whisk on high for 3-5 min until pale and tripled in volume; warming the eggs helps them hold more air. Fold in the butter and vanilla, then sift over the flour and cornflour and fold gently until no streaks remain. Divide between the tins.

steps.title: Bake the sponges
steps.text: Bake for 17-20 min until golden and a skewer comes out clean. Cool in the tins for 10 min, turn out and cool completely, about 1 h.

steps.title: Layer the cake
steps.text: Split each sponge into 2 layers with the serrated knife. Warm the jam and spread about 75 g on the cut side of each layer. Place one layer on the board, spread on about 120 ml custard, and repeat twice more, finishing with the last layer jam side down. Chill for 30 min.

steps.title: Shape the dome
steps.text: Whip the cream with the icing sugar and vanilla paste to stiff peaks. Coat the sides thinly, then heap the rest on top and smooth it into a high dome with the offset spatula. Chill while you roll the marzipan.

steps.title: Cover in marzipan
steps.text: Knead the marzipan until smooth, tinting it green if needed, and keep back a walnut-sized piece. Roll it between the sheets of baking paper to a 38 cm circle, lift it over the cake and smooth it down from the top, easing out folds. Trim the excess and tuck the edge underneath.

steps.title: Add the rose
steps.text: Colour the reserved marzipan pink, shape a small rose from thin petals and set it on top. Dust lightly with icing sugar and keep chilled until serving.

tips: Whip the cream really stiff; a common mistake is soft cream, which lets the marzipan slump.
Chill the cake between stages so each layer firms before the next.
Use a long serrated knife and a gentle sawing motion to split the sponges evenly.
Cut with a hot, dry knife for clean slices.
Don't taste the raw dough or batter: raw flour and raw egg aren't safe to eat until baked.
storage: Keep in the fridge, loosely covered, and eat within 2 days. Not suitable for freezing once assembled.
